newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, outlook unclear.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, outlook unclear.

text.p: Polish shares rose for the fourth session running, despite some expectations of a weaker market on Wednesday, and analysts said strong selling after price-fixing and rises in live trade made Thursday unclear.
They also said much could depend on the performance of the Dow Jones later on Wednesday after Tuesday's surge.
Analysts said the good Warsaw bourse mood, in part because of March's low 0.8-percent inflation figure, might be offset by a market that seemed fairly valued.
"The main market 1997 P/E for non-banks is about 19--that's pretty high," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski of Bank Gdanski house.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 1.8 percent to 17,016.3 points and turnover rose 42.9 percent to 249.9 million zlotys ($79.5 million) on all three markets. Gainers led losers by 62 to 13 with 18 stocks flat.
Analysts said some cash could be returning to stocks after Tuesday's heavy oversubscription of 7.5 million shares of paper firm Celuloza Swiecie at a special bourse session.
They said a negative sign this week could be the 222- million-zloty ($70.7 million) primary market offer by metals firm Impexmetal.
Analysts said trader Universal's 9.9 percent surge may have been triggered by the stock's piercing of a recent high in continuous trade on Tuesday.
Remak led the five construction firms that rose at least 6.7 percent, surging the daily maximum 10 percent with post-price-fixing demand strong enough to reduce players' bids.
